name: GitLab MCP
tagline: Manage GitLab repos, merge requests, issues, and CI pipelines from chat.
shortDescription: The official GitLab MCP server. Create and review merge requests, manage issues, trigger CI pipelines, inspect jobs, and read repository files. Works with self-hosted GitLab and GitLab.com.
longDescription:
## What it is

GitLab's official MCP server. Exposes the GitLab REST and GraphQL APIs as MCP tools: create/merge/close MRs, file and update issues, trigger pipelines, inspect job logs, list project files, manage milestones, and search across code.

## Why we recommend it

It comes from GitLab itself, so the auth, pagination, and rate limits all work as expected. Self-hosted GitLab is fully supported (point it at your instance URL), and the read-only mode is a great default for safe exploration.

## When to use it

- Triage: agent lists your open MRs and groups them by status/reviewer
- Issue creation: agent turns a chat conversation into a well-formed issue
- CI: agent inspects a failing pipeline, pulls job logs, and suggests fixes
- Code review: agent reads diffs and leaves inline-style comments
installInstructions:
1. Create a GitLab personal access token at https://gitlab.com/-/user_settings/personal_access_tokens (scope: `api`)
2. Set `GITLAB_TOKEN=glpat-...` and `GITLAB_URL=https://gitlab.com` (or your self-hosted URL)
3. `npx -y @gitlab/mcp-server`

**Self-hosted:** Set `GITLAB_URL` to your instance (e.g. `https://gitlab.mycompany.com`).
pricingDetails: Free. The MCP server is open source. GitLab is open source. GitLab.com is free for unlimited public repos.
